_about: Special advisers' declared interests published inside departmental annual reports and accounts (owner's job, 28 Oct 2026). Transcribed word for word from each report's special adviser interests section; line breaks joined with a space and words split across lines rejoined. Every entry was checked by machine against the text of the report's PDF page before loading. page is the page of the PDF file named in source_url (not the printed page number). Loaded into spad_interests; the Cabinet Office's standalone publication is parsed by lib/spad-background.ts instead.

reports.source_title: HM Treasury annual report and accounts 2025 to 2026

advisers.name: Shadi Brazell
entries: Ms Brazell is a Trustee of Cambridge House. She must recuse herself from any funding decision relating to her role as a Trustee of Cambridge House.
As of 14 May 2026 Ms Brazell has since left her position as Special Adviser at HM Treasury.

advisers.name: John VanReenen
entries: Mr VanReenen remains employed by London School of Economics (LSE). He splits his time between LSE and his position as Special Adviser at HM Treasury.
Mr VanReenen therefore recuses himself from all matters relating to higher education policy and funding.
As of 16 March 2026, Mr VanReenen has since left his position as Special Adviser at HM Treasury.

advisers.name: Anna Valero
entries: Ms Valero is on a career break from LSE, although she continues to be employed by them.
Ms Valero therefore recuses herself from all matters relating to higher education policy and funding.

Ms Valero has also declared her position as an elected council member of the Royal Economic Society Council. It is recommended that Ms Valero recuse herself from any funding or investment decisions related to this organisation.
As of 21 August 2025 Ms Valero has since left her position as a Special Adviser at HM Treasury.

reports.source_title: Defra's annual report and accounts 2025 to 2026

advisers.name: Jamie Williams
entries: Jamie Williams' brother held ministerial positions in the Cabinet Office and the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology.

advisers.name: Joe Corry-Roake
entries: Joe Corry-Roake held an unpaid role as a trustee for Grandparents Plus and was not included in discussions on any planning applications regarding Orchard Farm Kennington.

Mr. Corry-Roake was not included in discussions relating to the review of environmental regulation led by his father Dan Corry prior to publication; however, he was able to work on the recommendations.

advisers.name: Oliver Longworth
entries: Oliver Longworth’s partner held a Special Adviser post at Number 10 whilst he was a special adviser in the department. Mr. Longworth was advised not to discuss departmental business with his partner.

advisers.name: George Sanderson
entries: George Sanderson declared a previous employer, Hanbury Strategy, which has commercial interests in certain areas of the department’s work. Appropriate mitigations have been agreed and communicated to ensure Mr. Sanderson is not involved in advice or decisions relating to specific agreements or negotiations connected to this interest. Alternative special adviser cover is provided where appropriate.

advisers.name: Benjamin Szreter
entries: Benjamin Szreter resigned from roles as a company director and trustee of the Albion Foundation, and from the Lost Boys Taskforce, around the time of taking up the departmental role.

Mr. Szreter also declared family connections to organisations with potential commercial interests related to the department. Mitigations are in place to ensure Mr. Szreter is not involved in relevant contractual or commercial matters.

advisers.name: Eleanor Salter
entries: Eleanor Salter declared personal connections with civil servants in Defra and DESNZ and does not engage with those officials in one-to-one meetings in an official capacity.
Ms. Salter also declared that her partner is a journalist; mitigations are in place to ensure Ms. Salter does not respond to media enquiries involving that partner or discuss departmental business.

advisers.name: Sophia Kewell
entries: Sophia Kewell declared that a sister is employed by a company that is a supplier to the department. Mitigations are in place to ensure Ms. Kewell does not participate in discussions or decisions relating to contract awards involving that company.

reports.source_title: DHSC annual report and accounts: 2024 to 2025

advisers.name: Caroline Elsom
entries: Caroline’s partner is the Director of External Affairs at Waymap and is a Conservative councillor on Wandsworth Borough Council. He was the Conservative prospective Parliamentary candidate for Tooting constituency during the July 2024 General Election.
Caroline’s sister is a General Practice Specialist at Broad Lane Surgery.
Mitigation: Caroline would recuse herself from any involvement with interactions with the organisations above. Other than declaration no other mitigations were required.

advisers.name: Robert Ede
entries: Robert’s wife works in a government-facing role at Biogen UK.

Mitigation: Mitigations were in place including Robert not having any involvement with any dealings, discussion or advice related to Biogen and/or potential future contracts or bids. Robert also agreed to recuse himself from discussions of any report he authored before joining DHSC.

advisers.name: Peter Wilson
entries: Peter’s sister is a consultant paediatrician at St Richard’s Hospital. Peter’s brother-in-law is a GP partner at St Paul’s surgery, Winchester

Peter is the owner and sole director of PPW Consulting Limited, through which he conducted communications consulting work on a self-employed basis between November 2022 and December 2023, prior to his appointment as a special adviser.

Mitigation: Peter did not solicit new business or conduct any business whatsoever through the entity, or on behalf of or in concert with his former clients for the duration of his employment as a special adviser. Should any potential conflicts, or the perception of potential conflicts have arisen with respect to his former clients through his work as a special adviser, Peter would have declared this to the Permanent Secretary in a timely manner and recuse himself if appropriate.

advisers.name: Fergus Cameron Watt
entries: Fergus was recused from involvement in discussions or matters relating to Bain & Co.
